doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Blakey's delicate trio drumming versus his sextet power
summary: Brower contrasts loud drummers with cymbal-detail players; Walton says Blakey adjusted for trio work, as on Monk records.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Uh, coming back to something uh you touched on yesterday and the approach that Blakey had, you know, from loud power, loud bottom, and these drummers, lot of snare drum, which Blakey did play, but lot of, kind of details, lot of cymbal work, real different energy, real different way of shaping the music, coloring the music, and pushin' the music.

Yeah, well Art Blakey was the leader, so I mean, he emphasized in his own way and uh this context requires uh, uh, a slightly different approach, you know. A more uh, sensitive … not more sensitive, but uh, more delicate approach, shall we say, especially the trio playing. And uh, I heard some recordings with uh Thelonious Monk, and uh, Art Blakey and uh Al McKibbon, and you can hear Art's uh trio of uh playing on there, but that's all I can think of, recorded-wise. And you'll see, you'll hear a different Art than the bombastic with the sextet playing, larger groups.
